Recommendations_for_management_of_patien.anticoagulation: DOACs recommended in preference to VKAs in patients with HF, except in moderate or severe mitral stenosis or mechanical prosthetic heart valves; use CHA2DS2-VASc to guide anticoagulation, NOACs preferred over warfarin in non-valvular AF.
Recommendations_for_management_of_patien.rate_control: Beta-blockers recommended for short- and long-term rate control in patients with HF and AF; AV node ablation may be considered for refractory symptomatic patients.

Recommendations_for_management_of_patien.revascularization: Coronary revascularization considered to relieve persistent symptoms of angina in patients with HF and CCS; myocardial revascularization recommended when angina persists despite anti-anginal drugs.

Recommendations_for_management_of_patien.SGLT2_inhibitors: SGLT2 inhibitors (canagliflozin, dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, ertugliflozin, sotagliflozin) are recommended in patients with T2DM at risk of CV events to reduce hospitalizations for HF, major CV events, end-stage renal dysfunction, and CV death; empagliflozin may be considered in patients with T2DM to prevent or delay onset of HF and prolong life.

Recommendations_for_diagnosis_of_HF.coronary_angiography: Invasive coronary angiography may be considered in patients with HF and intermediate-to-high pre-test probability of CAD or presence of ischaemia on non-invasive stress tests.
Recommendations_for_diagnosis_of_HF.CTCA: CT coronary angiography may be considered in patients with low-to-intermediate pre-test probability of CAD to rule out coronary artery stenosis.

Recommendations_for_device_therapy_in_HF.ICD: An ICD should be considered to reduce the risk of sudden death and all-cause mortality in symptomatic HF patients with reduced LVEF despite ≥3 months of OMT and expected survival >1 year.
Recommendations_for_device_therapy_in_HF.CRT: CRT recommended for symptomatic patients with HF in sinus rhythm with QRS duration 130–149 ms and LBBB morphology and LVEF ≤35% despite OMT to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity and mortality; upgrade to CRT may be considered in certain paced patients.

Recommendations_for_management_of_patien.diuretics: Combination or loop diuretic strategies considered for patients with resistant oedema; adjust based on response.
Recommendations_for_management_of_patien.vasodilators: In selected hypertensive acute HF patients, IV vasodilators may be considered to improve symptoms and reduce congestion.
Recommendations_for_management_of_patien.short_term_MCS: Short-term mechanical circulatory support may be considered in refractory cardiogenic shock depending on patient age, comorbidities, and neurological function.

Associated Conditions: Cardiovascular events (hospitalization for HF, CV death)
